model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the development of three economic policy indices—“Wirtschaftspolitik insgesamt” (overall economic policy), “Finanzpolitik” (fiscal policy), and “Handelspolitik” (trade policy)—from 2016 to mid-2025. The x-axis represents time, spanning from 2016 to 2025, with tick marks at two-year intervals. Two y-axes are used: the left axis, labeled “Index,” ranges from 0 to 1,000 and is used for “Wirtschaftspolitik insgesamt” (black solid line) and “Finanzpolitik” (blue solid line); the right axis, also labeled “Index,” ranges from 0 to 9,000 and is used for “Handelspolitik” (purple solid line). The black line for overall economic policy fluctuates between approximately 50 and 500 until 2020, peaks near 500 in early 2020, then declines and stabilizes around 100 until 2024, before rising sharply to over 700 by mid-2025. The blue line for fiscal policy follows a similar pattern, peaking near 450 in early 2020, then falling to around 50–100 until 2024, and surging to nearly 700 by mid-2025. The purple line for trade policy remains near zero until 2024, then climbs steeply to nearly 9,000 by mid-2025, indicating a dramatic increase in trade policy activity or intensity in the final period shown.
